messages.content: אני רוצה לדעת את תחזית המזג אוויר לתל אביב. בוא נבדוק את זה עבור קווי רוחב וקו אורך.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning: The user wants weather forecast for Tel Aviv. They want to check using latitude and longitude. We need to call the function requests_get with appropriate parameters. Tel Aviv coordinates: latitude ~32.0853 N, longitude ~34.7818 E. Use Open-Meteo API. The function signature: requests_get with url, headers optional, timeout, params: latitude, longitude, elevation optional. We need to provide the URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint. The typical endpoint: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". We need to specify query parameters: latitude, longitude, maybe hourly or daily? The user didn't specify. We can provide a simple forecast: maybe daily temperature. Let's include daily parameters: "daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum". Also "timezone=Asia/Jerusalem". So params: latitude, longitude, daily, timezone. The function signature only includes latitude, longitude, elevation. But we can pass additional query parameters? The params field only lists latitude, longitude, elevation. It doesn't allow arbitrary. But maybe we can pass them as part of the URL? The function signature is limited. But we can still pass the URL with query string appended. The function expects params: {latitude, longitude, elevation}. But we can embed other query parameters in the URL string. So we can set url to "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=32.0853&longitude=34.7818&daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum&timezone=Asia/Jerusalem". Then params can be empty. But the function signature requires params object. We can pass empty object. So call function with url and params empty. Let's do that.
